newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul parliament sets new deadline for labour law.
newsitem.headline: Seoul parliament sets new deadline for labour law.

text.p: South Korea's main political parties on Friday gave themselves a new deadline of March 8 to come up with a blueprint for a compromise new labour law.

They had earlier agreed to reach a consensus by Friday on legislation to replace a labour law that sparked almost a month of wildcat strikes after it was rammed through parliament last December by the ruling New Korea Party.
"We apologise to the people that we have not forged a single final proposal due to differences on several sticking points," parliamentary leaders of the three parties said in a joint statement.
But they said it was important to find a consensus and added: "We agreed again to do our best to produce a single proposal by March 8."
The law passed in December is due to take effect on March 1. But the government has said it will not be enforced in its present form.
President Kim Young-sam was forced to return the legislation to parliament in the face of bitter opposition from labour unions and criticism at home and abroad.
